raw_response:
I'm 68 years old and only started farming on my own last year. Before that I was working outside in construction, but my body can't take it anymore, so I came back to the village. My wife and I are the only ones at home — our children are working in the city — so it's just the two of us to manage 10.1 mu. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those extension pamphlets. I watch what my neighbors do, especially Old Wang who has the plot next to mine, and I ask him when I'm unsure. Last year was my first year, so I mostly copied him, and things turned out okay. Not great, but okay.

This year I'm keeping most of my land in wheat-maize double cropping — about 7 mu — because that's what everyone around here does, and it gives us two harvests. The other 3.1 mu I'll plant cotton again. Cotton is hard work for an old couple because of all the picking, but the price was decent last year and we need the cash.

For the wheat, I'm planting in mid-October, around the 15th. I bought improved seed from the same shop in town as last year, 25 yuan per mu. I don't save my own seed because I don't know how to select it properly. For fertilizer, Old Wang uses more than me, but he has more money. I put down about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, and then I spread about 20 kg of urea at the same time. In the spring, when the wheat starts turning green, I'll topdress another 10 kg of urea if it looks yellow. I irrigate three times: once after planting if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Water from the well costs money — they meter it now — so I don't do more than that. I spray herbicide once after planting, and if I see aphids I'll spray insecticide. I expect about 380 kg per mu if the weather is normal. Last year I got a bit less because I was late with the topdressing.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 15th. There's never enough time — sometimes only four or five days — so I hire a tractor with a rotary tiller to prepare the field quickly. I buy hybrid seed, about 45 yuan per mu. I apply compound fertilizer at planting, about 20 kg per mu, plus 15 kg of urea. Then when the maize is knee-high, around the big trumpet stage, I add another 10 kg of urea. Two irrigations: one after planting if it hasn't rained, and one at the big trumpet stage. I expect around 420 kg per mu. Last year the maize did better than the wheat.

For cotton, I plant in late April. I use improved cotton seed, about 30 yuan per mu. I put down less fertilizer than for grain — about 15 kg of compound and 15 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice and I have to spray for bollworm because last year I lost some yield to insects. The problem with cotton is the picking. With just me and my wife, it's slow and hard on our backs. We do most of it ourselves, but if we're behind in September I might hire a few days of help. I hope for about 280 kg per mu of seed cotton, but it depends on the weather.

All together, my inputs will cost about 2,900 yuan this year. That's a lot of money for us. I can't afford more, so I have to be careful. I know I'm not using the "optimal" amounts, but I'd rather be a little safe than risk having no money left for medicine or emergencies.
